page_title: Posnic POS | Free Open-Source Offline Point of Sale

sources.entry: Posnic - Offline-first open-source POS and billing software for retail shops and restaurants. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Posnic/POS)

summary.name: Posnic POS
summary.one_liner: Posnic POS is an open-source, offline-first desktop point-of-sale and billing application for Windows, macOS and Linux, aimed at retail shops and restaurants, with optional paid cloud services.
use_cases: Run checkout and billing in a retail shop on one computer
Track sales, stock and returns for a small store
Operate restaurant table and kitchen order workflows
Try the POS before installing via the public supermarket demo
Evaluate an open-source POS for offline use
Add browser access or backup through optional cloud services
summary.what_it_does: The local edition is a desktop POS application installed on Windows, macOS or Linux that keeps its database and API on that computer and does not require a Posnic account. It covers sales, stock and reports from one system, with browser access available as an add-on. The source is published under AGPL-3.0-only, and a live demo runs the same code with admin, manager and cashier logins. The publisher reports receipt, report and scale-frame tests, but states that no physical printer, scanner, scale or payment terminal was connected in those tests. Optional paid cloud services are documented for sync, off-site backup and remote dashboards.
notable: Offline-first local edition with database and API on the local computer and no required account
Open source under AGPL-3.0-only with a public GitHub repository
Public live demo of the same code with admin, manager and cashier roles that resets hourly
Optional paid cloud services for browser access, extra counters, off-site backup and remote owner workflows
caveats: Cloud services are optional and paid; their current prices and boundaries are published separately
The recorded runtime workflow was reproduced on Windows x64 only, and no independent security audit has been commissioned
Hardware compatibility is not certified by Posnic for any named retail device; hardware, setup, support and downtime still carry cost
